newsitem.title: JAPAN: Daihatsu says dollar rate of 115 yen is best.
newsitem.headline: Daihatsu says dollar rate of 115 yen is best.

text.p: Daihatsu Motor Co Ltd said on Wednesday that the most appropriate dollar/yen rate for its business would be about 115 yen.
"About 115 is good for us," vice president Hajime Fujii told a news conference.
"We want currencies to stabilise," he said.
Daihatsu said it has assumed an average dollar/yen rate of 115 yen in setting its earnings forecast for 1997/98, compared with 112 yen the previous year.
Fujii said Daihatsu, Japan's second biggest minicar maker, plans parent capital investment of 43 billion yen in the year to March 1998, up from an actual 30.1 billion yen the previous year.
Daihatsu also forecast a parent operating profit of 19.5 billion yen for 1997/98, up 1.7 percent from an actual 19.18 billion yen in the previous year.
Fujii also said Daihatsu's parent depreciation costs will increase to 30 billion yen in 1997/98 from an actual 25.7 billion yen the previous year.
Daihatsu forecast domestic vehicle sales of 495,000 units in 1997/98, up 2.9 percent from the previous year.
It also expects vehicle exports to rise 36 percent from the previous year to 102,000 units in 1997/98.

Daihatsu is owned 33.4 percent by Toyota Motor Corp and assembles recreational vehicles for Toyota. It said it expects the number of these vehicles supplied to Toyota to rise 33.1 percent from a year earlier to 211,700 units in 1997/98.
